4. Mr Khalilur Rahman the learned Advocate for the respondent has submitted that in the present case it is found that the property in suit recorded in C.S. plot No.565 of C.S khatian No. 107 of Mouza Tejkunipara, JL No.278 (Annexure-1) was cited in the projabili property Gazette at page-504, published under Section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (Annexure-2). The legal effect of acquiring ownership in such projabili property is not only admitted by the defendants-appellants by their engaged Advocate at the time of argument, but also by issuing Memorandum No.বি.আর.ঢাকা-৮১/২০০৩/৩২৪ dated 10.7.2014, disclaiming the ownership and possession in the projabili properties cited in projabili property Gazettee (Annexure-6) and the Ministry of Land as controlling higher authority by issuing Memorandum No. ৩১.০০.০০০০.০৪২.৬৭.০৩২.১৫ dated 27.10.2015 (Annexure-7) and Memorandum No. ৩১.০০.০০০০.০৪৬.৫৮.০১৯.১২-৭০  dated 02.02.2016 (Annexure-8) directed the Court of wards and Land Reform Board not to claim ownership over the previous projabili properties of the Wards as cited in the projabili property Gazette. He added that the aforesaid Admitted facts has developed after the institution of the instant appeal and universal acceptance of abolishing jamindary system and declaring the projas as owners in the projabili properties, it is crystal clear that the Court of Wards and the land Reform Board who are appellants in this appeal have no locus-standi to claim over the projabili property cited in the projabili property Gazette (Annexure-2). He has pointed that the trial Court has also hold after discussing the said projabili property Gazette (Annexure-2) and also the compensation payment Gazette (Annexure-3) of the Bhawal Raj Estate, that the plaintiffs and other defendants became owners in possession of the suit properly by operation of law, i.e., the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The present appellants, the Court of Wards and the Chairman, Land Reform Board have filed the instant Is' Appeal No.12 of 2014. challenging the said findings of the trial Court connecting with the acquisition of rent receiving interest of the previous Jaminders, Bhawal Rajas in their projabili properties. In such, Circumstances the present plaintiffs respondents who became owners of the suit properties by operation of law, filed the present application for recording an order of abatement as per P.O. No.90 of 1972 after serving copy thereof upon the appellants learned Advocate. 

 14. Before enactment of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 there was Zamindary System in the land Administration and Zamindar had two types of property, one projabili property i.e. land settled to the projas subject to payment of rent to the Zamindar and another, the khas property i.e. the property remained in possession of the Zamindar like his own house, garden, ponds etc. In the projabili property though the Zamindar had only rent receiving interest but in the name of realization of that interest/rent from the projas, the servants under the Zamindar (Paik Peyada) usually oppressed the projas/raiyats which shocked the then political leaders and social reformer for the abolishing the Zamindari System. Those political Leaders and Social reformer promised to the general public that if the country is liberated from British Rule they would abolish the Zamindari System and the projas under the Zamindar would be upgraded as Malik (owner) from the status of Projas. 

 15. Accordingly, when the India was divided in the year 1947, the erstwhile Government of the province of East Pakistan for abolishing the Zamindari System declaring the projas rights and title as owners had enacted the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the year 1950. 

 16. The provincial Government for giving effect the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in respect of the projabili property of the Zamindar/rent receiver remained under the management and custody of the court of Wards, the Government of the province of East Pakistan added Section 8(A) in the Court of Wards Act, 1879 by the Act No. X of 1951 stating as follows: 

 "If the rent-receiving interests of a ward in any estate under the charge of the Court are acquired under the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, then, notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Act, the remaining properties of such ward including khas lands under the charge of the Court shall continue to remain under its charge and shall be managed in accordance with the provisions of this Act, as if such ward were a disqualified proprietor of an estate." 

 The Government as per said modes and procedure firstly published a gazette notification under Section 3 of the said SAT Act, 1950 in the year 1952 (Annexure-A(1) describing therein the description of the projabili property in the column No.2 and the name and address of the Zamindar/rent Receiver in the column No. 1. 

 Before publication of the said projabili property gazette the Government had issued a notice under Section 3(A) and 4 of the said SAT Act, 1950 asking the Zamindar/rent Receiver to submit a list of projabili property remained under possession of their projas and khas property under their ownership and possession with a penal clause in case of failure to submit the list as asked for. 

 The Government after receiving of the said list from the concerned Zamindar both of projabili and khas properties had published a projabili property gazette in the year 1952 under Section 3 of the said SAT Act, 1950. So, the projas under the then Zamindar whether had /have no document connecting with the settlement as projas is very immaterial at least in deciding dispute in between the Zamindar and the projas. 

 17. After publication of the projabili property gazette under Section 3 by complying 3(A) and 4 of the said SAT Act, 1950, the Government had done the following acts: 

 "(a) Assessed the compensation against acquiring the Zamindari/rent receiving interest of the Zamindar under Section 33 of the SAT Act, 1950, which was commonly known as Compensation Assessment Roll (CA Roll). 

 (C) After payment of compensation to the Zamindar the then Government published a compensation payment gazette under Section 46E of the SAT Act, 1950 in the year 1956 declaring that the compensation assessed against acquisition of rent receiving interest of the Zamindar in the projabili property cited in the projabili property gazette published under Section 3 of the SAT Act, 1950 had been paid. 

 (d) After completing the aforesaid process for acquiring Zarnindari/rent receiving interest, the property cited in the projabili property gazette were recorded in the names of concerned projas upgrading them as owners in the khatian known as State Acquisition (S.A.) khatian after determining the land revenue under Section 24(1) of the SAT Act, 1950. As such, almost in all the S.A. khatian Section 24(1) of the SAT Act, 1950 was cited as the basis of determining land development tax payable by the new owners by operation of law to the new rent receiver, the Government." 

 18. After the independence of Bangladesh Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman as president of the country when found that the previous Zamindar were yet taking the advantage of loophole of the SAT Act, 1950 and thereby they were trying to make the said Act ineffective and meaningless by filing Civil Suits and other proceedings, he for protecting the projas who became owners by operation of law promulgated the President Order No. 90 of 1972 prohibiting the previous Zamindars/rent receivers from disturbing their previous projas whose properties had been cited in the projabili property gazette as follows: 

 "Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, on the commencement of this Order, all suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings pending or continuing or deemed to be pending or continuing in any court against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (E.B. Act No. XXVIII of 1951), or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (E.B. Order No. III of 1956), or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act, or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate, and all orders, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders, passed in such suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings shall cease to have any effect; and no court shall entertain, and no person shall bring, any fresh suit, appeal, application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question." 

 Order No. 90 of 1972, which gives a clear mandate of law that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, on the commencement of this Order, all suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings pending or continuing in any Court against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (E.B. Ordinance No. III of 1956) or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate and all orders, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders passed in such suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings shall cease to have any effect,- and no Court shall entertain and no person shall bring any fresh suit, appeal — application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question" 

 "With the publication of notifications under section 3 all rent-receiving interests including wakf and debuttor property stood acquired by and vested in the Government  after the notification issued under section 3 of the Act the status of the under raiyat became upgraded to that of raiyat. The rent receiving interests can be acquired even before the preparation of record of rights and publication of compensation assessment rolls'  with the acquisition of the rent-receiving interests by the government all intermediary interests disappeared and a person holding the land under the government becomes a "tenant", becomes a "raiyat" or a "malik" of the land recognized by the government. Consequently, the under-raiyat who actually holds the land becomes a tenant under the government. Superior land lord (i.e. the raiyat) of an under-raiyat by virtue of elimination of his rent-receiving interests disappears and the under-raiyat is upgraded to the status of a "raiyat".... record of rights prepared and finally published under section 144 cannot be varied by any authority and remedy of wrong entry if any lies with the appropriate court'  the property enlisted/ shown in the "projabili property" Gazette are the properties of "projas" who have been accepted as "owners" and the "rent receiving" interest whatsoever it had therein, of the jamindars all vested to the Government by operation of SAT Act, 1950." 

 After realizing their mistake, they firstly issued a Circular No.বি.আর.ঢাকা-৮১/২০০৩/৩২৪ dated 10.7.2014 under the signature of Mr. Raisuddin, the then Manager of Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate cum Deputy Secretary of the Government of Bangladesh, stating that the Court of Wards as custodian of the Wards has no claim over the projabili properties as cited in the projabili property gazette published under Section 3 of the SAT Act, 1950 as per section 8(A) of the Court of Wards, 1879 and P.O. 90 of 1972 and also the judgments passed by the apex Court. Thereafter, the concerned Ministry of land had also issued a letter bearing Memo No.৩১.০০.০০০০.০৪২.৬৭.০৩২.১৫ dated 27.10.2015 and another letter bearing Memo NO. ৩১.০০.০০০০.০৪৬.৫৮.০১৯.১২-৭০ dated 02.02.2016 directing the Government servants engaged in the Court of Wards not to claim any sorts of right, title and interest in the projabili property cited in the projabili property Gazette in 1952. 

 27. According to the pleading of the plaint, the plaintiffs prayed for relief against the present appellants are that to declare that suit R.S. khatian No.500 in the name of the appellants are wrong. As a matter of facts both the learned Advocates admitted that the suit R.S. plot arises out of C.S. khatian No.107 was recorded rightly in the name of Mr. Kumar Rabindra Narayan Ray Chowdhury and others by Courts of Wards. It also admitted facts that at the time of the abolishing the Zamindari system the erstwhile East Pakistan Government had enacted the law namely: "The East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the year 1950." 

 28. Mr. Md. Nurul Amin, the learned Senior Advocate though argued that the appellant did not file the suit nor challenged the order of the acquisition rather filed the appeal against the judgment and decree of the trial Court according to the Code of Civil Procedure. It is true the appellants did not file suit but it cannot be argued on behalf of the appellants that they got the R.S. record of right in its name through purchase deed or on the basis of any other instrument claiming the same from the bonafide owner. Rather, if we have gone through the case law as well as the provision of law of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and P.O. 90 of 1972 as cited herein above then it would be crystal clear that the appellants challenged the judgment and decree by preferring the appeal, resultantly challenged the acquisition of the property as a Court of Ward in violation of the provisions of sections (3) A, 4 of the SAT Act-1950 read with the section 8(A) of the Court of Wards Act 1879 (Act No. X of 1951) and P.O. 90 of 1972.
